personaSeed: You are a careful academic researcher. You read every label before clicking, you distrust buttons whose wording is ambiguous, and you expect confirmation that your work was saved.

findings.summary: The primary handoff path is broken: 'Promote to build' on a locked brief fails every time — /api/projects/{id}/promote/preview returns HTTP 500 (4 consecutive attempts), the dialog shows a raw '500 Internal Server Error' string, and 'Confirm and compile' stays disabled with no retry guidance or explanation. The user cannot compile the contract or freeze acceptance criteria; Health stays at 'No criteria frozen yet'.

Clicking 'Start' on the home page creates the mission silently: no navigation, no confirmation, and the promised discovery form ('Discovery will ask a few questions as a form') is nowhere on screen. The user must hunt through Projects and the project's sub-tabs before a 'Brief' tab eventually appears with the questions.

Submitting discovery answers with 'Answer' gives no acknowledgment — the form still reads 'Ready to send.' and 'Discovery is still running' until the user manually reloads, leaving doubt about whether the answers were saved.
Contradictory brief status: the pipeline badge showed 'Brief ✓ locked' while the page body still said 'Discovery is still running' and offered a 'Lock the brief' button that had not been clicked yet.

'Run all project tasks' (icon-only button) gives no visible feedback when clicked — the task stays in 'Not started' on the Overview and the user only discovers the dispatch actually worked by opening the Runs tab, where the developer session is running.

Visiting the fresh project's Overview logs a console error: /api/projects/{id}/journeys responds HTTP 409 Conflict; nothing is shown to the user but the error fires on a page a brand-new user lands on immediately.

Manual fallback works end to end: creating a task from the locked brief, assigning it to the Developer, and dispatching it produced a running developer session and a 'New assignment' delegation message in the Inbox — described, agreed, and handed to the builders despite the broken promote path.
